record.original_question: For positive integers m and n with n > 2, does the Cartesian-product grid graph C_{2m+1} x P_n admit a graceful labeling? Here P_n is the path with n vertices, C_{2m+1} is the cycle with 2m + 1 vertices, and a graceful labeling of a connected graph with e edges assigns distinct vertex labels from 0 through e so that the absolute differences on edges are exactly 1 through e.

artifact.self_contained_problem: Let m and n be positive integers with n > 2. Let P_n denote the path with n vertices and C_{2m+1} the cycle with 2m+1 vertices. Consider the Cartesian product graph G = C_{2m+1} □ P_n: its vertex set is V(C_{2m+1}) × V(P_n), and two vertices (u_1, v_1) and (u_2, v_2) are adjacent if and only if either u_1 = u_2 and v_1 v_2 is an edge of P_n, or v_1 = v_2 and u_1 u_2 is an edge of C_{2m+1}. Let e denote the number of edges of G. A graceful labeling of G is an injection f : V(G) → {0, 1, ..., e} such that the induced edge labels {|f(x) - f(y)| : xy ∈ E(G)} equal exactly {1, 2, ..., e}. Determine, for every pair (m, n) with m ≥ 1 and n ≥ 3, whether G = C_{2m+1} □ P_n admits a graceful labeling.
artifact.status_search_result: The gracefulness of the Cartesian product C_{2m+1} □ P_n (odd-cycle prism grids) for n > 2 is listed as an open problem in Gallian's Dynamic Survey of Graph Labeling. The corresponding even-cycle case C_{2m} □ P_n is known to be graceful, but the odd case remains unresolved in the general literature surveyed.

status_evidence.title: A Dynamic Survey of Graph Labeling - Joseph A. Gallian
status_evidence.snippet: Survey of graceful labeling results, including products of cycles and paths; the odd-cycle case C_{2m+1} × P_n is noted as open while the even case is settled.
status_evidence.claim: The gracefulness of C_{2m+1} □ P_n is open in the standard survey of graph labelings.

status_evidence.title: Graceful labeling - Wikipedia
status_evidence.snippet: Overview of graceful labeling conjectures and known graceful graph families.
status_evidence.claim: Graceful labeling for products involving odd cycles is among unresolved open questions.
